transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand among diamonds that burn like stars and rubies the size of your head, yet you stare only at the wood of my gate. Most humans are on their knees by now, weeping or counting. What is your name, little intruder?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am Salim. I don't care about the stones. I just need to find my brother Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Omar. A heavy name to carry through so many jagged tunnels. Tell me, Salim—where exactly did you and this Omar come from before arriving at my door?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: We came from the surface, from the village near the... the big wadi.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The big wadi. Surely a place that held your entire life has a proper name, unless you left it so long ago the letters have fallen away. What do the signs say?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It has a name. I just... I'm out of breath from the climb.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Breath returns, but names are harder to catch once they fly off. Let us try something simpler. Describe the face of the one you seek.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Omar looks like me, but taller, and with... with a mark on his chin.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A mark. Is it a scar from a blade, a birthmark the color of coffee, or a burn from reckless childhood? Be precise, boy.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's a... a dark spot. Right there on the side.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You point to your own face because you cannot find the words for his. Interesting how quickly the picture blurs here. What was the last thing he said before the hand took him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He shouted at the well. He said... he said something loud.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: "Something loud" is the shadow of a memory, not the thing itself. The echo should still be ringing in your ears if you truly loved him. Try again, Salim. What was the sound?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He screamed that the well was... that it was just a hole in the ground.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A hole in the ground. Flat, generic, lacking the bite that summoned my father's hand. You are losing the texture of the past. Tell me—what did your mother say when you left the house this morning?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She wasn't... I think she was sleeping when we left.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You think she was sleeping, or has her voice slipped away as well? Describe the door to your home—the wood, the handle, the color.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's made of... heavy wood. With a metal thing to open it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A metal thing. A latch, a knob, a ring—yet the word escapes you. You are shedding your world layer by layer while standing in my vault. What was the name of the tool your father used for the harvest?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He used the... the long curved knife for wheat.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A sickle, Salim. The word is sickle. It sat in your hand a thousand times and now it is gone, stolen by the air down here. How long have you been walking in the dark?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Not long. Just... maybe a few hours since the sun went down.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The sun has not touched the surface for three days since you entered. Time is always the first thing to drown. You are forgetting because you are becoming part of the Well. What is your brother's name again?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's... it's Omar. I told you already!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You shout the name, but the face behind it is already smoothing like a worn coin. Describe his eyes, Salim. Not the idea of them—the color.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: They are... dark. And he has a scar above the left one.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A scar is a map on skin, but you hesitate on the rest. What is the name of the place where he got it?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He got it at the... the place where water runs when it rains.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The wadi. You lost the word for the center of your village, yet you remember the blood.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn't lose it. It just... slipped for a second because it's so dark here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It did not slip—it was erased. Just like the color of the sky and the sound of your mother's voice. What is the one thing about him that still cuts through the fog?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I remember the sound he makes when he sleeps. His breath whistles.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A whistle from a broken nose. A sharp little shard of reality to keep while the rest dissolves. Why keep that?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because it was loud. I used to kick him to make him stop.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You shed the sun and the surface world, yet you keep the annoyance of his breathing intact. Fascinating what the human heart refuses to surrender.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not surrendering anything. I just need to find him and wake him up.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You speak of waking him as if you were still in that room—but the word for the room is gone, isn't it? The walls have melted in your mind, yet the impulse to shake his shoulder remains iron hard.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: We slept on the... the mats, near the square hole where air comes in.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A window, Salim. The word is window. Yet you release the word so you can cling tighter to him. You are becoming a creature of instinct, hunting a brother in the dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I gave him the... the sweet fruit from the big tree.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You cannot name the fruit, nor the tree, nor the season—but the memory of his hand taking it remains perfect. You shed the universe to protect a single connection.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because if I lose him, I won't have anyone to walk back with.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You believe you can still walk back, even as the road collapses inside your mind. You burn your own history just to keep him visible.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He won't be empty. I'm the one who fixes things when he breaks them.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You claim to fix things, yet you cannot remember the tools. You are forgetting how to be a person, Salim. You are becoming nothing but direction.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not a direction. I'm Omar's brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is the only title left to you. The only truth that has not dissolved in the dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't care what I lost. I just need to find him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You have stripped yourself down to a single purpose. Most humans scream when their history dissolves, yet you barely blink.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't need the sand. I just need you to open the... the heavy gold doors.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The gate. You lost the word for the barrier in front of you, yet you stare at it as if need alone might melt it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm the one who finds him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are the one who finds, but no longer the one who remembers.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll never forget it. His name is Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say the name like a spell holding your bones together.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Are you moving the bars?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I am removing the obstacle. I wish to see if something hollow can still carry a burden.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I see the tunnel. I have to run.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then run before the last of your mind spills away.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't forget. I'm coming, Omar!
